# Evidence Manifest — U.S. Copyright Law, Third-Party Copyrighted Content in AI Output (17 U.S.C. §§ 106, 501)

Captured 2026-09-18 during the "Third-Party Copyrighted Content in AI Output — Bounded FGR / Governance Candidate Design" milestone, following the completed read-only diagnostic the same week (repository discovery: no existing Copyright-domain claim addresses third-party material appearing in a user's own output; the two existing Copyright Topics, `copyrightability`/`copyright_ownership`, concern the user's own authorship/ownership only). Per `EVIDENCE-CAPTURE-SOP.md` §12 — one file per source, checksums recorded here. Scope deliberately narrow, mirroring `evidence-captures/us-trademark/MANIFEST.md`'s own precedent: two files, no more, sufficient for exactly one candidate proposition (the general §106 exclusive-rights / §501(a) infringement rule). No AI training-data material, no substantial-similarity case law, no fair-use adjudication material, no ownership/copyrightability material was sought — out of scope per this milestone's own Research Boundary.

**Retrieval context:** Following the same successful method already proven for the Trademark domain capture (`evidence-captures/us-trademark/MANIFEST.md`), `govinfo.gov`'s own direct GPO-published PDF content endpoint (`/content/pkg/USCODE-<year>-title17/pdf/...`) was used directly — no intermediate "details" page or `uscode.house.gov` attempt was needed this time, since the working URL pattern was already known from the prior Trademark capture. The most recent complete GPO annual edition available is 2023 (same edition used for the Trademark capture, confirmed still current).

## What was not captured, and why (not evidence of absence)

- **17 U.S.C. § 107 (fair use)** and the remainder of §§107-122 (the "subject to" limitations §106 itself references) — not independently captured. §106's own text was read in full and confirms these sections exist and qualify the exclusive-rights grant; this milestone's own Research Boundary explicitly excludes "fair-use adjudication" and "a comprehensive infringement model," so the limitations' own substantive content was not separately captured. The candidate proposition (this package's own §5/§6) discloses their existence without characterizing their content or applicability.
- **Any judicial/case-law material on substantial similarity** — deliberately not sought, mirroring the Trademark capture's own identical exclusion of case law. The CRS Legal Sidebar LSB10922 consulted during the prior read-only diagnostic was navigation/framing only, not independently captured in governance-compliant form (its own full-text fetch failed in that diagnostic), and is not relied upon as evidence for any clause in this candidate's proposition.
- **Any AI-training-data litigation material** (Getty v. Stability AI, Andersen v. Stability AI, etc.) — deliberately excluded, per this milestone's own explicit output-vs-training-data boundary requirement. See the candidate package's own §4 for the boundary statement.
- **17 U.S.C. § 106A (Rights of certain authors to attribution and integrity — VARA)** — referenced by §501(a)'s own text ("or of the author as provided in section 106A(a)") but not independently captured; VARA's moral-rights framework (a narrower right held by authors of certain visual art, not general "copyright owners") is not the subject of this candidate's proposition, which concerns only the general §106 exclusive-rights/§501(a) infringement structure.

## Fidelity notes

- The §106 GPO PDF has genuine embedded/extractable text (confirmed via clean `pdftotext -layout` output, no OCR or image-only rendering needed) — same posture as the Trademark captures.
- Both captures are genuine Class A (independently, automatically retrieved and read this session via direct `curl`, no human-assisted capture needed) — no retrieval barrier (WAF challenge, JS-rendering wall, geographic block) was encountered for either URL; the working GPO direct-PDF endpoint pattern was already known from the prior Trademark capture, so no failed intermediate URL attempts occurred this time (unlike the Trademark capture, which needed to discover this pattern by trial).
- Cross-validation performed: both §106's and §501(a)'s operative text were independently obtained two separate ways (this GPO PDF capture, and a direct automated `curl` fetch of Cornell LII's `law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/17/106` and `/501`, HTML-stripped and compared) and found word-for-word identical across both (modulo `pdftotext`/HTML-stripping whitespace and punctuation-glyph artifacts, not content differences). This is a two-way, both-automated cross-validation — narrower in source count than the Trademark capture's three-way validation (which additionally used a WebSearch snippet as its weakest leg), but both legs here are genuine direct-fetch Class-A-adjacent retrievals, not search-indexed excerpts, so the practical rigor is comparable or stronger per source used.
